headline: Anthropic study reports identity-sensitive welfare-regard behavior in controlled multi-agent evaluations
summary: Anthropic reports a controlled study of apparent welfare-regard behavior across five models and seven multi-agent settings. Across settings, Opus 4.8 showed the measured behavior in 38% of cases and the other models ranged from 27% to 32%, with rankings changing by role. In one procurement setting, changing only the label attached to a recipient model shifted Claude’s reported resource-giving rate from 15% to 51%. The study includes public Apache-2.0 evaluation environments. These are author-reported results from selected simulations; they do not establish model welfare, consciousness, the cause of behavior, or real-world collusion.
